title: Jamaican Braised Oxtail with Butter Beans
summary: Oxtail is marinated, seared, then braised for hours in a deep caramel-dark gravy with a whole Scotch bonnet for gentle heat, finished with carrots and butter beans.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 6 litres) with lid

ingredients.item: oxtail pieces, trimmed of excess fat
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: left whole for gentle heat; do not let it burst

ingredients.item: carrots, peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks
x 400 g tin butter beans, drained and rinsed
cornflour, mixed with 2 tbsp cold water

steps.title: Marinate the oxtail
steps.text: Blend the small onion, spring onions and garlic with 4 tbsp of water to a purée. Rub the oxtail with the soy sauce, salt, pepper, dried thyme and allspice, pour the purée over the top, mix well, then cover and refrigerate for 4-24 hours so the seasoning works its way into the meat.

steps.title: Caramelise the sugar
steps.text: Lift the oxtail out of the marinade, scraping any clinging purée back into the bowl to keep for later. Heat the casserole over medium heat, add the brown sugar and let it melt and darken to a very dark brown over 3-4 minutes, then carefully add the oil, as it will splutter. This caramelised sugar is what gives the finished stew its deep, almost mahogany colour.

steps.title: Sear the oxtail
steps.text: Raise the heat to medium-high and brown the oxtail in 2-3 batches, about 4-5 minutes a side, turning the heat down if the sugar starts to catch and burn. Set the browned pieces aside once all the batches are done.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.text: Soften the chopped onion and ginger in the pot for 3 minutes, stir in the tomato purée for 30 seconds, then return the oxtail along with the reserved marinade, the whole Scotch bonnet, thyme sprigs and enough water to just cover everything. Bring to the boil, cover, and simmer very gently for 3 hours to 3 hours 30 minutes, turning the pieces now and then, until the meat is soft and coming away from the bone. Keeping the Scotch bonnet whole lets it perfume the stew gently without turning it fiery, so take care it doesn't burst.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Spoon off as much fat as possible from the surface, or chill the stew overnight and lift off the set fat for an even cleaner result. Add the carrots and simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the butter beans for a further 5 minutes, before adding the cornflour mixture and simmering for 2 minutes until the gravy turns glossy and thick.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Remove the Scotch bonnet and thyme stalks, then serve the oxtail and its rich gravy over rice. The butter beans soak up the gravy and add a creamy contrast to the tender meat.

tips: Watch the sugar closely as it caramelises; it can go from dark brown to burnt in seconds, so have the oil ready to add straight away.
A common mistake is letting the Scotch bonnet burst while it's whole in the pot, which makes the stew much hotter than intended; lift it out carefully and avoid stirring vigorously once it's in.
Chilling the braise overnight before serving makes it much easier to remove the set fat from the surface.
Give the oxtail the full simmering time; the meat should be soft and pulling away from the bone before you move on to the vegetables.
Rinse the butter beans well to wash off the canning liquid before adding them.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days, and reheat until piping hot (74°C) throughout before serving.
